Subject: Reserved capacity SKU packaging and channel uplift clarity

Hi Megan / Tyler —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick follow-up with two asks so we don't misalign on the PO and marketplace listing:

1) SKU packaging: Orchid's procurement team requested that we present the reserved capacity as a single multi-sku bundle (base compute + burst credits + support hours). For marketplace listing / private offer, do we need separate Marketplace SKUs for each component, or is a single bundled SKU acceptable for passback calculations? Attached is the draft PO (Orchid_PO_draft_v2.pdf) and a preliminary sku_mapping.xlsx that maps our internal RC SKUs to how we thought they'd appear on AWS/GCP marketplaces.

2) Channel uplift / reseller margin: Orchid has a reseller partner that expects a 12% net margin on resold consumption. We typically model a 10% channel uplift on private offers for reserved capacity to keep list price competitive while preserving margin. Need confirmation from ops/sales: if we set a 10% uplift on the listed private-offer price, will partner passback math still reconcile with marketplace crediting rules (e.g., when Orchid redeems marketplace credits against committed usage)?

Immediate asks: can Ben and Connor confirm the recommended uplift range and whether we should split components into separate SKUs for invoicing and passback? Megan / Tyler — is Orchid comfortable with a 10% uplift as a starting point, or do you need a target list price from us to share with procurement?

Thanks — I copied our marketplace ops leads so we can move quickly.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Naomi / Connor / Megan —

Quick proposal from pricing/marketplace ops after reviewing the attachments:

Summary:
- Keep the public private-offer price as a single bundled SKU for ease of acceptance on Orchid side and to minimize friction in the AWS/GCP UI.
- Provide an invoice-level breakdown (three lines: base RC compute, burst credits, premium support) that mirrors the bundled SKU. This gives the reseller line-of-sight into margin.
- Apply a 9.5–11.5% uplift band on the bundled list price (midpoint 10.5%). The band accounts for regional tax/shipping and marketplace fees. For Orchid specifically, recommend we set the uplift at 10.5% so partner net remains >=12% after typical crediting.

Passback mechanics / notes:
- When Orchid redeems marketplace credits, cloud marketplaces apply credits against listed invoice amounts; because we expose the invoice breakdown, the partner passback will be calculated on actual redeemed amounts.
- We should include a short line in the private-offer terms that the bundle is eligible for marketplace credits and that passback calculations use the invoice-level allocation. That prevents disputes during reconciliation.

Deliverables I can produce today: a sample invoice PDF and a one-sheet passback worked example showing calculations for committed vs. overage usage. Connor — I need confirmation on whether billing can support issuing invoice-line adjustments tied to a single PO (i.e., bundle -> three invoice lines that sum to the private-offer total).

If billing can do that, I recommend we present Orchid with: bundled private-offer price (public on marketplace), invoice breakout, uplift 10.5%, and a short passback appendix.

Ben

Operations confirmation:
- Billing system: can emit a single invoice that contains the bundle total and the three invoice lines (base RC compute, burst credits, premium support) as requested. That will be the canonical source for passback math.
- Marketplace listing: AWS/GCP accept a single private-offer SKU mapped to multiple invoice attributes. We'll include a metadata mapping so reconciliation teams can tie redeemed credits to invoice lines.
- Taxes/fees: if Orchid is in the US and uses marketplace credits, credit application timing can shift partner net by ~0.5–1.2% depending on state tax. Recommend we keep uplift at 10.5% and include a small buffer clause in the appendix to handle tax variance.
